children: Lawson 5 near the western edge of the Prairie Evaporite has confirmed an active, generative Natural Hydrogen system in a 30-km step-out from the first four wells within the Lawson Complex near Central Butte in south-central Saskatchewan. Drilling at Lawson 6 is now in progress 8 km to the southeast.

Concurrent with continued discovery-focused drilling, MAX Power has commenced its completions program beginning with the Bracken target in the southwest corner of the province to be followed shortly by the start of comprehensive testing at Lawson in an attempt to confirm the world’s first large-scale commercial discovery of a new primary energy source.

(CSE: MAXX; OTC: MAXXF; FSE: 89N) (“MAX Power” or the “Company”) is pleased to report that drilling at “Lawson 5”, a 30-km step-out from the original Lawson Natural Hydrogen Discovery near Central Butte, Saskatchewan, has confirmed the presence of a Natural Hydrogen system along the western edge of the Prairie Evaporite, and a follow-up well (Lawson 6) is now in progress approximately 8 km southeast of this new discovery.

The scale of the Natural Hydrogen opportunity in Saskatchewan is highlighted in part by the fact that MAX Power has now confirmed active, generative Natural Hydrogen systems in three distinct areas separated by as much as 365 kilometers across the central and southern part of the province, from the western edge of the Prairie Evaporite southwest through the Lawson Complex (Lawson 1 to 4) to the Bracken target in the far southwest near the Montana border. A completions program has also just commenced at Bracken and crews will head north next week to begin testing the Lawson Complex for flow, concentrations, and volume as MAX Power’s commercial validation program intensifies.
Lawson 5 was successfully cased after being drilled to a total depth of 2,175 meters and will form part of the upcoming Lawson completions program (62 meters of core recovered for analysis);

The lowermost Deadwood and Precambrian basement complex at Lawson 5 features much more pronounced iron redox, alteration and serpentinization reactions than observed to date at Lawson, including strong hematite oxidation, associated with elevated levels of Natural Hydrogen along sub-vertical faults within a package of exotic terrane source rocks;
The Lower Interlake, above the Deadwood Formation, features helium prospective zones that will be examined for potential testing during completions.
Mr. Steve Halabura, MAX Power Chief Geoscientist, commented:

“MAX Power’s pioneering work in Natural Hydrogen continues to excite and amaze our geological team. Whether we’ve hit an entirely separate Natural Hydrogen system at L-5, or whether this is connected to the Lawson Complex, will be determined through more drilling and geophysical work we’ll be undertaking to optimize our understanding of the local and regional faulting and fracture systems. Lawson 5 skirted the edge of the Salt Wall. Lawson 6 to the southeast has a greater probability of drilling right through the Prairie Evaporite.”

“At the Lawson Complex we are continuing to review copious amounts of data ahead of the near-term start of completions. It has become increasingly apparent that at Lawson 4, we hit the Natural Hydrogen ‘kitchen’, but a kitchen that is potentially even bigger and more robust than originally believed. We look forward to providing an update on Lawson 4 and the broader Lawson Complex shortly.”
Mr. Rob Norris, MAX Power CEO, commented:

“This further expansion of the Natural Hydrogen opportunity in Saskatchewan speaks to both the favorable geology in this resource-rich province and the dedication and skill of our entire team. We’re excited to see what Lawson 6 brings as we also commence the completions round beginning at Bracken, something we’ve been eagerly anticipating for months. All of this is occurring as we approach the start of the world’s largest Natural Hydrogen conference (H-NAT) in Paris, France, where I’ll be joined next week by several of our team members as MAX Power is a significant sponsor of this event.”

MAX Power's latest results are reinforcing a much larger geological opportunity than a single Natural Hydrogen discovery. With active, generative systems now identified at the Lawson Complex and in significant step-outs at Lawson 5 (next to the Prairie Evaporite) and at Bracken in the southwest corner of the province, an area spanning 365 kilometers, the Company is building evidence for the potential of Natural Hydrogen deposits across a basin-scale exploration corridor. Importantly, these geographically separated discoveries support the broader exploration thesis while providing additional targets for technical evaluation.

The commencement of completions at Bracken, followed immediately by comprehensive testing at Lawson, represents a critical next step. MAX Power is moving beyond confirming the presence of Natural Hydrogen toward measuring the characteristics that will determine its commercial potential: Natural Hydrogen concentrations, sustained flow rates, reservoir pressures, connectivity and ultimately recoverable volumes and production economics. The aggressive, back-to-back program is designed to generate important technical data across multiple targets while drilling continues to investigate the potential for new discoveries.

At the same time, MAX Power is advancing the broader commercial strategy required to potentially bring a new primary energy source to market. Alongside its technical program, the Company continues to evaluate infrastructure requirements, prospective energy markets and opportunities for future commercial development. This parallel approach reflects MAX Power's “Months to Molecules” strategy: Advancing geological discovery, commercial validation and potential routes to market together, rather than sequentially.

For investors, the significance is the convergence of these developments. MAX Power is expanding its understanding of the regional Natural Hydrogen opportunity while beginning the testing needed to establish whether that geological potential can translate into commercially viable energy production.

MAX Power is an innovative mineral and energy exploration company focused on the shift to decarbonization. The Company’s Lawson Discovery near Central Butte, Saskatchewan, represents Canada’s first-ever subsurface Natural Hydrogen system confirmed through deep drilling with data validated by three independent labs. MAX Power has built dominant district-scale land positions across Saskatchewan with approximately
2.5 million acres (~1 million hectares) of permits

covering prime exploration ground prospective for large-volume accumulations of Natural Hydrogen, and has commenced a multi-well follow-up drill program to validate the commerciality of the broader Lawson Complex interpreted to cover a 28 sq. km area along the 475-km Genesis Trend. MAX Power also holds a significant equity position in Homeland Critical Minerals, which now owns the Willcox Project in Arizona, a lithium discovery confirmed in early 2024 by MAX Power. MAX Power is committed to responsible exploration and development practices that prioritize environmental stewardship, meaningful community engagement, and strong corporate governance.
